title: Secure a ponytail with a plain hair elastic
instruction: Gather the loose hair into a ponytail and secure it with the plain elastic. Leave it held after both hands let go.
setup: An upright 180 x 156 x 230 mm adult practice head on a 190 mm neck stand and 150 x 150 mm base, with twelve loose 24.5 cm synthetic-hair locks rooted across a 72 mm patch at the back. A separate plain silicone elastic, 30 mm inside diameter, with 3 mm cord thickness, rests on two 6 x 16 x 60 mm wooden rests, 33 mm apart between centres. Both grippers have narrow 40 x 4 x 3 mm finger extensions. Nothing joins the locks together or attaches the band to a hand. Restore the photographed layout.
scoring: 1.0 if at least 11 of the 12 locks pass through the elastic, the elastic is no wider than 5 cm and sits 2.5–16 cm below the head centre, and the ponytail remains held for three seconds after release. 0.5 for at least 9 locks through an elastic at that height; 0.25 for at least 6. Otherwise 0. Detached hair or a broken elastic scores 0. Judge the visible locks, band position and released video with a ruler.
fidelity: Twelve flexible lock bundles approximate loose hair; a native elastic surface models the plain band. Closing fingers must enclose the cord before a native point pinch can form. It releases on opening, 8 mm slip or estimated 6 N local tension; the force estimate is uncalibrated. Only the held patch has finger collisions filtered to avoid conflicting constraints. Hair remains free to bend, escape or snag. No point, hair or band pose is prescribed.
scores: Development diagnostics only; no validated full-score demonstration or Dream baseline yet.
context: A useful grooming skill combines gathering loose hair with stretching and releasing an elastic around it.
